subject: sociology
title: What Is School For?
welcome_lead: Why do societies make us sit in classrooms? Explore the functions of education and the hidden lessons schools teach.
meta_desc: GCSE Sociology adventure on the functions of education, hidden curriculum and the role of schools.
final_note: You can now explain what schools officially do — and the quieter lessons they sneak.

walkthroughs.body_html: Durkheim said school is a 'society in miniature'. Subjects like history teach a shared national story, creating social solidarity so children feel part of one community.

Parsons argued school is the bridge between the family and wider society. At home you are judged on particular ties; at school you are judged by universal rules — preparing you for jobs and a meritocratic society.
Bells, queues, uniforms and obedience all teach pupils to accept authority. Critics say this prepares workers to obey bosses, not to think freely.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between reliability and validity in research?
options: Learning facts in primary school.
Reliability is whether a method produces consistent results when repeated; validity is whether it actually measures what it claims to. A method can be reliable but invalid, or valid but unreliable.
Reliable and valid mean the same thing — that the research is good.
Reliable research is published in journals; valid research isn't.
